title: Hazel Dispatch POC — composite profile and cost-gating
body:
Executive summary:

This doc summarizes a 10-day bench run for Hazel (customer: Hazel Logistics) where we evaluated latency, throughput and token-level cost for a mixed read/write dispatch workload. Goal: quantify tradeoffs for hosted vs. dedicated vs. private deployment modes and recommend concrete cost-gating and routing strategies for production P95/SLOs.

Background and workload profile:
- Workload: dispatch assistant that ingests contextual short documents (avg 120 tokens) and returns multi-turn planning responses (avg 420 tokens generated). Mixed synchronous (70%) and async batch rerank (30%). Peak QPS target: 400 requests/s. Target p95 latency ≤ 450ms for short-path responses (first token), overall p95 for full generation ≤ 1.8s.
- Test traffic shapes: steady-state (250 qps), peak burst (400 qps sustained for 3m), microburst (1200 qps for 30s). Sequence length distributions: 20% short (<64), 50% medium (64–256), 30% long (>256).

Test matrix (representative runs):
1) Hosted API — rwd-1.3B (fp16) on shared H100 pools, default batching/autoscale
2) Dedicated — rwd-1.3B on reserved A100-80GB nodes, continuous batching tuned (max_batch=64)
3) Private (on-prem) — llama-13B-4bit QAT quantized on 8xA10g private cluster, KV cache enabled
4) Fallback variant — rwd-0.6B for extreme overloads (fast but lower quality)

Key metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (first token and full completion), tokens/sec (aggregate), effective QPS, GPU util, median and 95th tail CPU usage on control plane, token cost estimate ($ per 1M output tokens), cold-start time, and cold cache penalty.

High-level results (representative numbers):
- Hosted (rwd-1.3B, H100 pool): p50 first-token = 42ms, p95 first-token = 180ms, p95 completion = 980ms at steady 250 qps. Under microburst 1200 qps, p95 completion spiked to 2.9s with 20% error rate (429 throttling). Token cost approx $9.8 / 1M output tokens (including infra share).
- Dedicated (rwd-1.3B, A100 reserved, tuned batching): p50 first-token = 38ms, p95 first-token = 150ms, p95 completion = 740ms at sustained 400 qps. Survived 1200 qps microburst by shedding to fallback model via routing policy; p95 completion for primary when not shed = 1.1s. Token cost approx $3.6 / 1M output tokens (inc reserved amortized).
- Private (llama-13B-4bit, on-prem A10g): p50 first-token = 95ms, p95 first-token = 420ms, p95 completion = 1.9s at 200 qps (GPU mem limits prevented higher concurrency without sharding). Token cost estimated $1.9 / 1M (infrastructure fully customer amortized) but quality regressions noted on complex planning prompts (BLEU/ROUGE-style proxies decreased ~12% vs rwd-1.3B).
- Fallback (rwd-0.6B): p95 completion < 400ms at 1200 qps; used for graceful degradation on overloads.

Observed failure modes and root causes:
- Cold-KV penalty: first requests after a node recycle had 350–600ms jitter added for long sequences due to KV warm-up. Warmup reduced cost by preloading top-10 prefixes but required 2x traffic to be effective.
- Queue saturation microbursts: hosted shared pools applied throttles causing 429s; dedicated nodes handled bursts better but needed proactive admission control to avoid GPU queue depth blowouts.
- Quantization quality gap: llama-13B-4bit showed substantive output divergence on nested instruction prompts. Not strictly a perf issue but impacts cost/quality calculus.

Cost gating and routing experiments:
We ran policy experiments to maintain SLOs while optimizing cost:
- Policy A (latency-first): route to dedicated primary; use hosted fallback if dedicated overloaded; never route to private unless explicitly enabled. Outcome: best tail latency, cost ~2.9x hosted baseline.
- Policy B (cost-first): route short-path (<64 tokens) to rwd-0.6B hosted; medium/long to private quantized; use dedicated for priority customers only. Outcome: 35% cost reduction vs dedicated-only but p95 completion for long requests increased by ~320ms.
- Policy C (hybrid gating): maintain token budget per minute; when projected cost > budget, auto-apply soft QPS throttle plus degrade to fallback model for non-priority requests. Outcome: preserved p95 for priority traffic, overall 22% cost savings.

Concrete recommendations (short list):
1) SLOs & routing: adopt hybrid gating (Policy C) as default for Hazel with priority tagging. Implement per-customer token budget window and a soft QPS throttle that first switches non-priority routes to rwd-0.6B.
2) Autoscale & warmup: add proactive warmup on dedicated nodes before peak windows (start 10m prior). Warmup script used in bench: bench/warmup.sh (linked). Cold-KV mitigation lowered p95 by ~180ms in experiments.
3) Batching knobs: for A100 dedicated pools, use max_batch=64, batch_timeout=8ms; for hosted H100 use conservative max_batch=48 to reduce tail jitter.
4) Fallbacks: implement a structured fallback plan with two levels — quality-fallback (rwd-0.6B) and async-fallback (accept request, return job id). Use fallback heuristics based on request length and priority tags.
5) Observability: add token-level cost attribution per route; capture per-model effective tokens, model-hours, and cache hit ratio.
6) Private deployment caveat: if Hazel wants sub-$2 token costs via private cluster, require model validation step and an evaluation guardrail for quality regression.

Example commands and harness notes:
- Load generator: k6 script (bench/scripts/hazel-k6.js) with ramp: 0->400 qps over 2m, hold 3m, microburst subtest uses wrk2 for short bursts.
- Sample perf call (curl): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-1.3B","prompt":"<ctx>","max_tokens":420}'
- Metrics collection: GPU telemetry via nvidia-smi + Prometheus node exporters, token accounting via request middleware (tags: customer, priority, model).

Next steps & owners:
- Implement Policy C prototype in staging (owner: Ravi Singh) — due 2028-10-20.
- Add warmup hook to dedicated deploy pipeline and test warmup window variability (owner: Liam Chen) — due 2028-10-18.
- Run a focused quality eval comparing rwd-1.3B vs llama-13B-4bit on 500 held-out planning prompts (owner: Marisol Ortega) — due 2028-10-25.

Appendix (selected raw numbers):
- Dedicated run 2028-10-07 (400 qps steady): GPU util avg 72%, p95 completion 740ms, overall success 99.7%, tokens/s 85k.
- Hosted microburst 2028-10-09 (1200 qps 30s): throttles 20%, p95 completion 2.9s, error 2.1% 5xx.
- Private bench 2028-10-05 (200 qps): p50 first-token 95ms, mem pressure prevented concurrency >220; observed OOM on long sequences if batch >1.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working POC doc; numbers are from controlled lab runs and will change under production integration. Please check linked artifacts for raw CSV logs before citing. Feedback requested on policy thresholds and whether we should surface a product feature (token budgets) to Console as a Beta for customers like Hazel.

-- Ava Morales (solutions-eng)
